newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria expects to reach 4.94 pct growth target.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria expects to reach 4.94 pct growth target.

text.p: Nigeria expects to achieve it's budgeted target of 4.94 percent growth in 1996, finance minister Anthony Ani said on Thursday.
"A substantial measure of macro-economic stability has been achieved during the six-month period," Ani said in his half-yearly review of budget performance up to June 30.
He did not give a figure for growth in the first six months of the year.
"The level of inflation is now under control as a result of stable macro-economic policies."
Ani said inflation had declined from 72.8 percent in December 1995 to 55.3 percent in June 1996.
The battle against inflation has been the keystone of Nigeria's tight fiscal policy in both 1995 and 1996.
In the delayed February 1996 budget speech military leader General Sani Abacha set a target for year-on-year inflation of 20-30 percent.

The figures the finance ministry uses to calculate inflation are based on rolling averages of the previous 12 months. The Federal office of Statistics put year-on-year inflation for May at 31.0 percent, the last figure to be made available.
Ani said inflation had now fallen to a level below which the government's cap on bank interest rates was no longer relevant.
"The interest rate pegged at 21 percent appears to have fallen as it is reported that some banks have been lending at between 18 and 19 percent," he said.
